topic: Bone fusion: babies have about 300 bones, adults 206
hook: Babies have about 300 bones. You have 206.
caption:
You were born with roughly 300 bones, and you've lost about 94 since. Nothing went missing, though. They fused together as you grew.

Your skull started as several plates with soft gaps, so you could fit through the birth canal and your brain could grow. Some bones keep fusing into your twenties.

Follow for one body fact your brain won't believe, every day. Tag someone who just had a baby 👶

Cover: Babies have about 300 bones. You have 206.
🎨 AI-generated image

1/4 Built to fuse (300)
Many baby bones start as separate pieces of cartilage. As you grow, they harden and fuse into fewer, bigger bones.
📷 Evan-Amos (Public domain) via wikimedia

2/4 The soft spot (24 mo)
A newborn's skull is several plates with gaps between them. The big soft spot on top usually closes by 18 to 24 months.
📷 BruceBlaus (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia

3/4 Five become one (5→1)
Your sacrum, at the base of the spine, starts as five separate vertebrae. They fuse into a single bone by adulthood.
📷 Wasiul Bahar (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia

4/4 Most hide in hands, feet (106)
Your hands and feet hold 106 of your 206 bones. That's more than half your entire skeleton.
📷 Mikael Häggström (CC0) via wikimedia
